value.rationale: The degree-two cycle is the canonical connected one-dimensional regular habitat and a natural boundary to the motivating higher-degree dynamical percolation study. The result gives all-size exact uncertainty for survival counts, a sharp one-sided extinction density step, and a parameter-critical loss of genuinely macroscopic synchronized biomass oscillations even though occupied density is continuous at equality. These features are substantial dynamics/statistics of the model, not just a parameter substitution or isolated numerical example.
